structured_output.verdict: Not ready. The library-side docs and tooling changes look mostly right. The website integration has blocking defects: provenance and version matching, broken published redirects, a likely wrong manifest path in build-vendor, and a full suite that isn't green on a clean import. The website's own AGENTS.md says merging to main deploys the site and MCP, so the integration branch can't merge while rc2 is unpublished and deployment is unauthorized.
blockingIssues: The website full suite is 83/86 against a stale export. The fix is 'awaiting clean import', so nothing has been re-verified. Re-run the full suite plus the 27 focused checks and the stdio/worker parity check on a clean export of the exact library commit before treating anything as passing.

Deployment gate: the website's AGENTS.md says a merge to main publishes the site and MCP. This branch replaces the canonical, indexable /docs/ corpus with unpublished rc2-candidate content while npm and the homepage runtime are rc1. Merging it now is an unauthorized deployment and gives rc1 consumers docs for a different contract. Keep it on a branch, or deploy the candidate to a non-canonical noindex host (for example the v5 mirror) until rc2 is published.

site/_redirects deletes the /development, /troubleshooting and /development/manifest.json redirects outright. Those were published URLs. They now 404 instead of pointing to the new pages (/docs/quick-start/, /docs/tooling/, /docs/manifest.json). The old redirect targets are gone too, so repoint them rather than delete them. This also contradicts the file's own comment 'Published preview URLs remain supported'.

scripts/build-vendor.mjs now reads node_modules/marionette/dist/docs/manifest.json. The production harness and CONTRIBUTING both put the packaged manifest at the package root as docs-manifest.json. Unless rc1 shipped a different layout, this path is wrong and the vendor build will fail or read the wrong file. Check it against the installed rc1 tarball and add a test.

Version matching is unsafe if versions are reused. The skill, agents.md and MCP guidance only require a sourceRevision comparison 'for a source candidate'. If the candidate export carries a version that is also published (no version bump is authorized), a consumer with published rc1 installed matches on version alone and gets candidate contracts. Either make the revision (or contentSha256) comparison unconditional, or have MCP reject version-only matches when the catalog status isn't published. Confirm which packageVersion the exported manifest actually carries.
risks: Candidate status is conflated with the npm dist-tag. readSnapshot hard-requires manifest.channel === 'latest', and publishedChannel requires publication.channel to equal it. So an unpublished candidate is advertised as channel 'latest' in the corpus and catalog, while the new guidance says never to use a latest alias.

publicationStatus is a free choice from a three-value allowlist in publication.json and isn't tied to any evidence. 'release candidate (published on npm)' can be paired with sourceDirty:true or an unpublished version. Derive it, or at least enforce: sourceDirty or an unpublished version means 'development candidate (local source)'; published statuses need a registry or tarball hash check at import.

In mcp/load.mjs, the records example's `runtime: provenance` labels it with the docs snapshot identity. That's right for the source, but the workshop recipes that used to be served are dropped from MCP with no replacement. Agents following /agent-prompt.md (rc1 workshop) can't retrieve the matching recipe through get_example. Say this explicitly or fence it.

The plugin path in docs/agents.md tells consumers to add 'this checkout' as a marketplace. npm consumers have no checkout. The plugin's skill scripts come from whatever revision is checked out while reading the installed package's manifest, so script and manifest formats can drift.

The external install links (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills, developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins) aren't covered by docs:check, and the website's coverage limitations say external URLs aren't checked. They're unverified and may not exist.

context7.json drops packages/data and packages/adapters. If companion-package docs aren't mirrored under docs/, Context7 loses them. Confirm the navigation's 'Companion packages' section sources live under docs/.
bundleGroups matches section names exactly. A navigation section missing from every group silently drops its pages from all task bundles (it still appears in llms-full).
Harness: release-evidence.json is optional. Without it the report binds no evidence, yet it can still read as 'passed'. Release use should require it.

Harness cache check: buildB replaces buildA, so there's no test that old hashed assets survive a deploy for tabs still open. The local no-cache/etag check doesn't establish CDN or Pages behavior, and the report limits say so correctly.

Client activation: only Codex has real discovery evidence. Claude Code 2.1.119 validates the manifest but full cache activation is unverified, and Cursor is unverified. Don't describe either as working.
incorrectAssumptions: 'Local candidate remains identified as a candidate' is only true until merge. The branch's own deploy-on-merge contract makes the website change a publication step.
Passing checks against a stale export aren't evidence for the clean import. The 76 page-width checks and the 80 docs / 1 record / 244 calls parity numbers must be re-run on the exact import.

The 'close pending startup then reopen' browser check doesn't show stale-response suppression. control.aborted is counted but never asserted, and the test clicks Open right after settlePending without checking that the late response left the torn-down UI alone.

'No source aliases' isn't asserted. The harness copies the delivered vite.config.js and checks realpath only for the package roots. It doesn't check that resolved modules in the build come from workspace/node_modules.
pageerror-only capture doesn't cover 'asset/API errors'. Unexpected 4xx/5xx responses and requestfailed events (other than the deliberate 503) aren't collected.
missingTests: build-vendor reads the rc1 docs manifest from its actual packaged path and rejects a mismatched one.
Redirect table: every previously published /development*, /troubleshooting* and /reference/*.md URL resolves to a live page (no 404 chain).
publicationStatus consistency: rejects a 'published' status when sourceDirty is true or when the version doesn't match an installed or registry tarball hash.
MCP rejects a request whose version matches but whose revision differs, or the guidance mandates the revision check. Test whichever contract you choose.
Every navigation section is assigned to exactly one bundle group, and every tasks[] route exists (fail with a clear message, not a TypeError on undefined).
Harness: assert control.aborted > 0 or equivalent after close, or assert no list or status is rendered after settlePending and before reopen.
Harness: collect response.status >= 400 and requestfailed events, allowlisting only the intentional failure-mode API call.
Harness: after switching to buildB, assert that the previous build's hashed assets still return 200, or document that the host must retain them.
Harness: make release-evidence.json required in release mode, and assert the Vite build graph resolves only under the workspace.
readSnapshot rejects leftover assets (troubleshooting, benchmarks, ROADMAP) and passes with the consumer-only set. Confirm the old fixtures were deleted, not just left unreferenced.
simplifications: Drop `symbols.mjs` from the readSnapshot asset regex. The docs say exact-symbol lookup isn't distributed.
Remove the dead maintainer branches in sidebar and page render: the /maintain|release|histor|archive/ collapse regex and the 'Maintaining Marionette' Audience filter. The corpus is consumer-only now.
